text:
maria: Quick Q — we're rolling header-based feature gates next week. For older SDKs that don't send the new 'X-RW-Gates: v2' header, do we want the server to 1) auto-fallback to v1 flags, and 2) emit a telemetry event so we can monitor rollout coverage?

jonathan: +1 for fallback -> server returns the best-effort feature set. Also emit a metric 'gate_negotiation_mismatch' with tags: sdk_version, client_region, endpoint. Keep it sampled (1%) by default.

sam: Agree. For the SDK change, opt-in header should be added in 2.5.0. Implementation note: header name we decided was 'X-RW-Gates' and value 'v1' or 'v2;client=2.5.0'. Example:
```
X-RW-Gates: v2;client=2.5.0
```
If server sees unknown value, fall back to v1 and return:
```
X-RW-Gate-Set: v1
```

carla: Guardrail suggestion: if mismatch rate > 5% for a canary cohort for > 10m, auto-pause rollout and alert #eng-oncall + release-triage. Also add a debug-level log with request id. :warning:

maria: Sounds good. Also want to capture which specific flags were missing in the response for partial compatibility checks. Maybe add 'gate_mismatch_detail' as a sampled event payload (string list). Keep payload size small. 

jonathan: Implementation detail — store mismatch count in our per-customer rolling window (1h), expose in Console under 'Rollouts > Gate Negotiation' with % mismatch and top-3 missing flags. 

release-bot: canary created: rw-client-canary-2026-03-17 (5% traffic) — assigned to @maria, @sam. 

maria: I'll open a PR for server handling + metric + console panel. Ping me for review: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/1234 — will add unit tests for header parsing and telemetry sampling. 

sam: I'll cut SDK 2.5 branch tomorrow and include header and opt-in flag. Will also add a runtime fallback that logs a single warning per process for unknown header variants. 

carla: One more — add a short doc blurb in Release Checklist about feature negotiation and how to interpret Console graphs. tiny PR ok. :memo:

maria: Thanks all — moving to async. If something urgent ping me or @eng-oncall. :tada:
